title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rises to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes in GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: The archive limits, eligible licences, automatic increase and PowerShell controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. The briefing correctly distinguishes the government rollout window from Learn's October dates and the roadmap's launched status. The licence-review checklist has a minor controls-table coverage gap.

claims.claim: Eligible Exchange Online auto-expanding archive mailboxes gain a maximum capacity of 3 TB instead of 1.5 TB.
claims.quote: Eligible archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can automatically expand beyond the current 1.5 TB limit, up to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators cannot adjust the auto-expanding archive storage quota.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Once auto-expanding archiving is enabled for the organisation, it cannot be turned off.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.claim: Once auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, it cannot be turned off.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search also search the additional storage areas of an auto-expanded archive.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: When a mailbox is placed on hold, content in its auto-expanded archive is also on hold.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: No new permission or identity is described for the capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: auto expanding archive increase 3 TB new permissions identity enable automatically 560820 Worldwide. Read MC1521615 and both cited Learn pages; they describe the existing enablement roles, not a new identity or permission for the increase.

claims.claim: A global administrator can enable auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving, you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.claim: A member of the Exchange Online Organization Management role group can enable auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving, you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.claim: For specific users, membership of a role group containing Mail Recipients suffices.
claims.quote: Alternately, to enable auto-expanding archiving for specific users, you must be a member of a role group that includes the Mail Recipients role.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports cloud-based archive mailboxes in Exchange hybrid deployments.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving for the organisation.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving for a specific user.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, run the following command. ... Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for enabling organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving enable Exchange admin center Microsoft Purview portal tenant user PowerShell. Opened purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving: 'You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving.'

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for enabling auto-expanding archiving for a specific user.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving enable Exchange admin center Microsoft Purview portal tenant user PowerShell. Read purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving; it requires Exchange Online PowerShell and explicitly rules out enabling the feature in either portal.

claims.claim: The per-user enablement command is supported when both primary and archive mailboxes are cloud-based.
claims.quote: If a user's primary and archive mailboxes are both cloud-based, then you can use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for that specific user.

claims.claim: For an on-premises primary mailbox and cloud archive, the organisation-wide command is required instead of Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment, you have to run the Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive command in Exchange Online PowerShell to enable auto-expanding archiving for the entire organization.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks organisation-wide enablement.
claims.quote: To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell. Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks enablement for a user.
claims.quote: To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell. Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement does not set individual user mailboxes' AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property to True.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Enabling auto-expanding archiving for a specific user on hold or assigned a retention policy adds 10 GB to the primary archive quota.
claims.quote: When you enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user and the user's mailbox in on hold or assigned to a retention policy ... The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: The cited Learn archive pages do not explain what happens to an archive above 1.5 TB when its eligible licence is removed.
claims.quote: Searched: auto expanding archive 3 TB eligible license removed downgrade over 1.5 TB. Read both cited Learn archive pages in full and search excerpts for archive mailboxes and Exchange Online Archiving; none describes removal of eligibility from an archive already exceeding 1.5 TB.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends reviewing licence assignments for users with large archives.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends updating documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends reviewing licensing and retention strategies for users not eligible for the increase.
claims.quote: Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Once an auto-expanded storage area exists, users cannot delete folders from the archive.
claims.quote: If an archive mailbox has at least one auto-expanded storage area, users can't delete a folder from the archive mailbox or from the auxiliary archive.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving prevents recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving prevents you from recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.

claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to review licence assignments, but the controls table contains no corresponding licence-assignment row.
claims.quote: Review licence assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility; Microsoft's notice recommends this. The two controls rows govern only organisation-wide and specific-user auto-expanding archiving.
claims.fix: The Before rollout licence-assignment review has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the supported licence-review recommendation in Why it matters. Do not add a new control row in this correction.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
